title: Antoine dance and the unfamiliar piece Robichaux produced
summary: A ten-piece band at Antoine plays a request from Robichaux's music bundle; the requester turns out to be a guest from a rival band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Did they play at the Southern Yacht Club, was that, or where?
Oh, they wasn't at the, at the Yacht Club then. There's some club they used to play every night.

West End Roof, wasn't it? Huh? West End Roof, wasn't it? I think it was. I think that's the name of it. They had so many different places I'd get confused if I'm trying to take a show. Yeah, anyway, West End. Yeah, there's a player there, and they used to come on. They still sound good on that water, at night in band, that music still sound nice out there. Late at night, you know. And you could play too. They could play. We'd come on in. We'd catch a call right there in the West End call and bring us in town. And we was playing at Antoine one night. We used to play a big dance there, you know. And we had ten pieces that night. Yeah, Robeshow got a couple more other pieces. And we was playing there. And a fella come and asked for a piece of music. And Robeshow, he had a big bundle of music. He went down there and got a couple of pieces out. The man said, he said, take a look at it. We're going to play that next piece. The man, he told the man, first he told the man, I'll look and see if I got it. You know, he had so many he couldn't remember himself. So he had it. And he put it up there. And we started off. It's nice. And ten piece of band, you know, I thought I could hide, you know. Sometime you can get by on certain things, but you keep your eye on that music, you know. And if they get too hard for you, you kind of get over that and catch the next, you know. So I played that night and there was a party in there for the trambones, you know. And that's the first time I'd seen the piece of music. So when I got there, I missed it. Of course the fellas in the band, I don't guess they know the difference, you know. So, alright, you have to come back, play the encoder, play it again. I missed it again. I missed it. It's a, it's a, it's a very, it teaches a piece of music. But they never know, you see. So when I finished, a fella came up to me and said, that's a nice piece you all played. I said, yeah. He said, you missed something in there, didn't you? I said, I sure did.
Yeah, you know. You know who it was when I come to find out? It was a fella that played in that hour band.

But I had been hearing it. He's good, too. He's good. He said, well I'll tell you, he said, that piece give me some. He said, I'd listen for you to come out and see if you missed it. He said, I'll miss it, too. And I thought he'd get it down, you know. I thought he got it down and he'd miss it too.
This is the first time you ever saw it. You did pretty good to keep going.
Yeah. When you're playing like that, if you can keep up with the music, you skip. If you miss, yeah, don't miss over there. If you get out, you're out altogether, you see.
This was a, was this Neto? Was that his name? Who? Neto, the trombone player was out. I think it was, yeah.
Now he was a guest at that. He had on his tuxedos and everything. He was a guest at that day.
